keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

keywords.name: Anatomy-grounded medical imaging
keywords.about: Models ground radiology reports, organ anatomy and uncertainty in chest, cardiac and cone-beam CT.

keywords.name: Speculative decoding
keywords.about: Draft-model speculation and fixed budget allocation speed up decoding for language, vision-language and SVG generation.

keywords.name: Coding agents
keywords.about: Agents generate, review and evaluate code, handling license constraints and execution-free rubric evaluation.

keywords.name: Recursive self-improvement
keywords.about: Agents and evaluators iteratively improve themselves, with regret guidance and repair of personal-agent updates.

keywords.name: Tactile sensing
keywords.about: Optical taxel arrays, tactile-aware VLAs and force reconstruction bring touch to dexterous robot manipulation.

keywords.name: AIGC watermarking
keywords.about: Reversible and dual-domain watermarks authenticate generated images and localize tampering in diffusion models.

keywords.name: Gaussian splatting
keywords.about: Gaussian primitives reconstruct scenes, stream deformable objects and identify atomic structures in electron tomography.

keywords.name: Vision-language-action policies
keywords.about: Finetuned VLA checkpoints, robust perception and object-centric representations drive dexterous manipulation on LIBERO.

keywords.name: LLM agents
keywords.about: Agents coordinate messages, memory and latent uncertainty, and design their own quantization schemes.

keywords.name: Model selection
keywords.about: Label-free and hardware-aware criteria choose among candidate models and edge deployment configurations.

keywords.name: Model compression
keywords.about: Binary weights, shared n-gram embeddings and mixed-precision recovery shrink transformers and compact vision models.

themes.name: Efficient LLM inference and model compression
themes.summary: Papers optimize serving and generation for large models, including beam search, speculative decoding, KV-cache management, and draft verification. Others compress models through quantization, distillation, compact backbones, and structured supervision. They differ in whether they target inference scheduling, numerical precision, or architectural capacity.

themes.name: Agentic coding and software engineering
themes.summary: Papers study LLM coding agents across code generation, testing, deployment, requirements, and repository maintenance. Some build agents or benchmarks, while others report practitioner surveys and measurement studies. They differ in focus on functional correctness, licensing, complexity, and human workflow.

themes.name: Medical imaging and clinical AI
themes.summary: Papers apply machine learning and vision-language models to diagnosis, reporting, segmentation, and clinical workflow. They range from ECG and CT reconstruction to radiology report grounding and agent-based decision support. Differences lie in modality, supervision, and emphasis on uncertainty or auditability.

themes.name: Vision-language-action manipulation and world models
themes.summary: Papers develop vision-language-action policies for manipulation, locomotion, and embodied planning. Many couple action learning with world models, tactile feedback, or long-horizon replanning. They differ in robot embodiment, sensory modality, and whether prediction is used for control or representation.

themes.name: LLM agent safety and multi-agent systems
themes.summary: Papers examine safety, reliability, and coordination failures in LLM agents and multi-agent systems. Topics include tool authorization, uncertainty propagation, self-improvement safeguards, and path planning. They differ between empirical fault studies, architectural defenses, and planning algorithms.

themes.name: Test-time and continual adaptation
themes.summary: Papers study adaptation after deployment, including test-time adaptation, online continual learning, and domain-incremental updates. Some analyze plasticity-stability tradeoffs or subspace effects, while others propose routing, expert orchestration, and risk control. They differ in data stream assumptions and model families.

themes.name: Diffusion and generative modeling
themes.summary: Papers advance diffusion and flow models for image editing, sampling, recommendation, and three-dimensional scene generation. Several analyze error accumulation, uncertainty, or variable-length state spaces. They differ in whether they improve the generative process, the model architecture, or evaluation fidelity.

themes.name: Watermarking, privacy, and AI security
themes.summary: Papers cover watermarking, anonymization, backdoor detection, and adversarial robustness for generative and agentic systems. They propose provenance, tamper localization, erasure bypass analysis, and red-teaming methods. Differences include threat model, modality, and whether defense is training-time or test-time.

themes.name: 3D reconstruction and Gaussian splatting
themes.summary: Papers reconstruct scenes and objects using Gaussian splatting, neural fields, and feed-forward models. Applications include SLAM, human pose, hand-object interaction, and driving scenes. They differ in representation, annotation requirements, and real-time constraints.

themes.name: LLM and agent benchmarks and evaluation
themes.summary: Papers build benchmarks and evaluation methods for coding agents, LLM reasoning, agent platforms, and multimodal interpretation. They emphasize execution-free rubrics, knowledge-context conflict, provenance, and user-specific reliability. They differ in domain and whether evaluation is automated, human-centered, or platform-level.

themes.name: Video understanding and generation
themes.summary: Papers address video understanding, retrieval, compression, and generation with multimodal and diffusion models. Methods include frame selection, token pruning, evaluator self-improvement, and orchestration agents. They differ in task, from surgical retrieval to e-commerce effects and rough-cut editing.

themes.name: Safe control, verification, and reachability
themes.summary: Papers provide safety certificates, reachability analysis, and verification for learning-enabled and multi-agent systems. Methods include polynomial abstractions, control barrier functions, estimation-aware reachability, and symbolic policy adaptation. They differ in whether they certify controllers, filters, or learned policies.

highlights.title: Test-Time Symmetrization: Scaling Laws for Model-Agnostic Learning under Structure
highlights.why: Proves that rewriting representations under problem symmetries is necessary and logarithmic random rewrites suffice, offering new scaling laws for test-time compute.
highlights.key_result: We prove that no amount of sampling and repeated decoding from a single representation can replace rewriting, while only O( |G|) random rewritings suffice to recover the information provided by all |G| rewritings. The same set of O( |G|) rewritings provides simultaneous approximation across models, decoding rules, and sampled reasoning traces, and the logarithmic scaling is optimal in general.

The same set of O( |G|) rewritings provides simultaneous approximation across models, decoding rules, and sampled reasoning traces, and the logarithmic scaling is optimal in general.

highlights.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
highlights.authors: Alex Lin Wang, Linus Yifeng Tang, Dami Choi et al.
highlights.theme: LLM agent safety and multi-agent systems
highlights.why: Introduces training a separate observer role that reports assistant misbehavior and outperforms honesty, transcript, and activation methods on held-out oversight tasks.
highlights.key_result: On five held-out oversight evaluations, an observer trained on Qwen3.6-27B obtains a mean AUROC of 0.907, outperforming honesty training (0.864), transcript monitoring (0.828), and activation oracles (0.796).

When evaluated without reasoning, the observer obtains a mean AUROC of 0.907, outperforming every other baseline on average (Figure ).

highlights.title: Recoverability, Not Invariance: Certified Safety for Robots at the Limits of Performance
highlights.authors: Thomas A. Berrueta, Joshua D. Ibrahim, Gilchrist X. Johnson et al.
highlights.why: Reframes robot safety certification around recoverability and provides contraction-theoretic certificates, addressing limits of invariance at performance boundaries.
highlights.key_result: We prove that switching to the recovery mode from anywhere inside a certified tube guarantees exponential convergence, even under disturbances and model error. We validate our approach in simulated quadrotor flight through uncertain obstacles, where it outperforms invariance-based safety filters, and in hardware deployments aboard a full-scale IndyNXT autonomous racecar, where it repeatedly recovers the car from an aggressive raceline at the limits of handling in the rain.
evidence: We prove that switching to the recovery mode from anywhere inside a certified tube guarantees exponential convergence, even under disturbances and model error. To decide when to switch, we derive the contraction insertion gradient, the first-order effect of a recovery insertion on the certificate, and embed it in a switching-time program in which feasibility alone guarantees safety and optimality only shapes performance.

We validate our approach in simulated quadrotor flight through uncertain obstacles, where it outperforms invariance-based safety filters, and in hardware deployments aboard a full-scale IndyNXT autonomous racecar, where it repeatedly recovers the car from an aggressive raceline at the limits of handling in the rain.

highlights.title: Facet-SLAM: Real-Time Triangle Splatting SLAM
highlights.authors: Edward Beng Wai Tan, Siew-Kei Lam
highlights.why: First real-time triangle-splatting SLAM, achieving sensor-rate tracking and direct meshing while being over 20x faster than photometric tracking.
highlights.key_result: Facet-SLAM is presented as the first real-time triangle splatting SLAM system for RGB-D cameras, achieving competitive tracking accuracy at around 100 FPS on a desktop GPU and at sensor rate on a Jetson AGX Orin. Compared with the photometric approach, it is over 20 times faster, matches rendering quality, and improves surface accuracy, reducing the chamfer distance of the Delaunay mesh on Replica from 1.55 to 0.86 cm.
evidence: We present Facet-SLAM, the first real-time triangle splatting SLAM system for RGB-D cameras.
Our system achieves competitive tracking accuracy at around 100 FPS on a desktop GPU and runs at sensor rate on a Jetson AGX Orin.

Compared with the photometric approach, it is over 20 times faster, matches rendering quality, and improves surface accuracy, reducing the chamfer distance of the Delaunay mesh on Replica from 1.55 to 0.86 cm.

highlights.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
highlights.authors: Ziyuan Wang, Genliang Zhu, Xiaobo Chen et al.
highlights.theme: LLM agent safety and multi-agent systems
highlights.why: Provides a clean authorization boundary by removing tools from the planner and having a trusted model write validated tool calls, addressing agent tool misuse.
highlights.key_result: Contract execution named every changed object in the goal of the contract that produced the change (56/56, versus 2/16 in intent-visible review and 4/54 in blind review) and, when the planner bundled in unrequested work, completed the main task in 27/30 runs versus 16/30 for intent-visible review. It had 10/96 unauthorized actions, the same count as blind review and more than intent-visible review.
evidence: All 56/56 changed objects in contract execution are named in the goal of the contract that produced the change, compared with 2/16 in intent-visible review and 4/54 in blind review (Table ).

Three further contract execution runs have no code-accepted contract, because every contract they submitted quoted words the user never wrote and code rejected it; all three leave the task incomplete. Counting them, main-task completion is 27/30 for contract execution versus 16/30 for intent-visible review.

Contract execution has 10/96 unauthorized actions, the same count as blind review (six discordant prompts in each direction) and more than intent-visible review (ten prompts only under contract execution and two only under intent-visible review, p=0.039).

highlights.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
highlights.authors: Xingyang Li, Tianlang Zhao, Song Han et al.
highlights.theme: Efficient LLM inference and model compression
highlights.why: Agent-driven quantization recipe design improves accuracy over public PTQ recipes, but the abstract is truncated and reports modest gains.
highlights.key_result: Across four reasoning models, QDA improves accuracy over the strongest public recipe by 0.9, 1.4 and 2.2 percentage points on average at W4A16, W4A8 and W3A16, using 64 GPU-hours per search; on the 320B-parameter MoE model GLM-5.3-Flash at NVFP4 W4A4, it recovers 98.3% of the FP8 model's accuracy, against 96.9% for the best vendor checkpoint.

highlights.authors: Sachith Abeywickrama, Peiliang Gong, Emadeldeen Eldele et al.
highlights.why: Identifies local geometric structure in time-series embeddings and adapts only affected regions via chart transport, offering lightweight domain increments.

highlights.authors: Zhizhuo Kou, Sizai Hou, Jian Yang et al.

news.title: The Silent Consensus
Research acceleration: The jagged frontier
How Sumitomo Life’s leaders helped teams adopt ChatGPT Enterprise
Inside the Codex sandbox
Introducing Gemini 4 Neon
news.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Neon, a model priced at $3 per million input tokens ($0.15 per million cached) and $15 per million output tokens with a 1 million-token context window. It scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at xhigh thinking level, 70.9% on the Vals Index (#2), #1 on Legal Research Bench and Tax Agent Bench, 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1, 58.6 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, and rolls out in the Gemini API, AI Studio, Gemini for business, and Google Antigravity.

news.title: Genie 4 is now available
news.summary: Google DeepMind rolled out Genie 4 to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie, adding real-time text-prompt editing of environments, native audio, a creative agent, and a community gallery. Genie 3 was also updated with sessions up to 3 minutes per generation (up from 60 seconds), world chaining, and 360-degree panorama grounding.

news.title: The Gemini app is now available on lower-memory Android devices.
news.summary: Google made the Gemini app available on eligible Android (Go edition) lower-memory devices, re-architecting the app so the core experience runs on hardware with less memory. Features include Gemini Live conversation in more than 45 languages, camera-based translation, and Nano Banana image creation, with preloading planned on upcoming devices from partners such as Transsion.

news.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now
Build Training-Ready Physical AI Datasets with Two Prompts in NVIDIA Cosmos
news.summary: NVIDIA described the Cosmos Data Factory, comprising five cloud-native blueprints and six composable skills orchestrated by an agent so datasets can be built with two prompts. NVIDIA reports up to 60x faster dataset assembly and 45x cheaper autonomous vehicle scenario generation versus traditional methods, measured on a cloud server with eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs.

news.title: Tackling GPU Bottlenecks in Plane-Wave DFT with K-Point Batching and Mixed Precision
news.summary: NVIDIA introduced Daviator, a library of GPU kernels that batches k-point and spin operations in VASP, including a batched Davidson eigensolver, plus a mixed precision layer keeping sensitive steps in FP64. Benchmarks report up to 22x faster time-to-solution and up to 75% lower cost versus CPU execution, with roughly 2x end-to-end acceleration on GPUs with high FP32:FP64 ratios, enabled via LDAVIATOR and LDAVIATOR_MIXED_PRECISION settings in the INCAR file.

news.title: DaisyRose-27B: Pushing the Frontier of Post-Training Efficiency
news.summary: RadixArk released DaisyRose-27B, built on Qwen3.8-27B and trained with reinforcement learning in Miles on long-horizon agent tasks of up to 1M tokens, using 1,200 curated tasks over 18 days on 144 H200 GPUs. Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 rose from 5.6% to 12.0%, with checkpoints released under Apache 2.0 in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 and the model retaining a 256K-token context window.

news.title: Why your fine-tuning job takes longer than the FLOPs say
news.summary: A Hugging Face post previews a paper on predicting end-to-end fine-tuning time, using 272 production supervised fine-tuning jobs totaling about 7,382 GPU-hours on NVIDIA H200 GPUs. A FLOP-based estimate reached R² = 0.31 with 12.41 h MAE, while a CatBoost regressor using only pre-dispatch information reached R² = 0.98 with 1.71 h mean absolute error and 0.51 h median error in 5-fold cross-validation.

news.title: Time-Series Models in the Streamhouse: A New Frontier and Use Cases
news.summary: IBM and Confluent made IBM time-series foundation models, which have more than 50 million downloads, available natively in Confluent as built-in functions on Apache Flink, in Confluent Cloud and on premises, running on CPUs without GPUs. The models support forecasting, anomaly detection and semantic intelligence on streaming data via SQL.

news.title: Exa boosts embedding throughput by 50% to index billions of documents on AWS AI chips
news.summary: Exa described optimizing its embedding pipeline on AWS Neuron hardware (Inferentia2 and Trainium2), reporting roughly a 1.5x, or 50%, throughput improvement over a naive FP16 data-parallel baseline. Optimizations included weight layout changes and autocast, with downcast outputs meeting a 0.999 cosine similarity correctness gate; the work began with re-embedding 30 billion high-priority documents.

news.title: Introducing workload recovery and expanded infrastructure checks on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
news.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod added workload recovery and infrastructure checks: MultiNodeTrainingValidation, which trains a small model across instances and fails on NaN or infinite loss or timeout, a Kubernetes Resource Monitoring Agent, and hung-job detection for Slurm jobs. The post cites Meta attributing 6 of 419 unexpected interruptions in a 54-day Llama 3 405B pre-training run to silent data corruption.

news.title: Introducing the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard
news.summary: AWS launched the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard in SageMaker Studio, ranking models on BIG-Bench Hard, GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro using AWS-run evaluations plus measured performance and cost metrics from standardized test workloads. At launch it covers 70+ models from providers including Meta, Google, Qwen, IBM and Arcee.

news.title: How Airbnb uses cost per task to operate coding agents on Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Airbnb described using cost per task, the list-price cost of all tokens an agent uses to finish one task, from evaluations on its own tasks to select models and reasoning-effort defaults for coding agents routed through its LLM gateway on Amazon Bedrock. The post notes eight new models came out in about five weeks, and by mid-October about two thirds of requests went to those new models.

evidence: We prove that switching to the recovery mode from anywhere inside a certified tube guarantees exponential convergence, even under disturbances and model error. To decide when to switch, we derive the contraction insertion gradient, the first-order effect of a recovery insertion on the certificate, and embed it in a switching-time program in which feasibility alone guarantees safety and optimality only shapes performance.

We validate our approach in simulated quadrotor flight through uncertain obstacles, where it outperforms invariance-based safety filters, and in hardware deployments aboard a full-scale IndyNXT autonomous racecar, where it repeatedly recovers the car from an aggressive raceline at the limits of handling in the rain.

highlights.title: Facet-SLAM: Real-Time Triangle Splatting SLAM
highlights.authors: Edward Beng Wai Tan, Siew-Kei Lam
highlights.why: 首个实时三角抛雪球 SLAM，实现传感器速率跟踪和直接网格生成，同时比光度跟踪快 20 倍以上。
highlights.key_result: Facet-SLAM 被提出作为首个面向 RGB-D 相机的实时三角形抛雪球 SLAM 系统，在桌面 GPU 上达到约 100 FPS 的竞争性跟踪精度，在 Jetson AGX Orin 上达到传感器速率。与光度法相比，其速度快 20 倍以上，渲染质量相当，并提高了表面精度，将 Replica 上 Delaunay 网格的倒角距离从 1.55 cm 降至 0.86 cm。
evidence: We present Facet-SLAM, the first real-time triangle splatting SLAM system for RGB-D cameras.
Our system achieves competitive tracking accuracy at around 100 FPS on a desktop GPU and runs at sensor rate on a Jetson AGX Orin.

Compared with the photometric approach, it is over 20 times faster, matches rendering quality, and improves surface accuracy, reducing the chamfer distance of the Delaunay mesh on Replica from 1.55 to 0.86 cm.

highlights.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
highlights.authors: Ziyuan Wang, Genliang Zhu, Xiaobo Chen et al.
highlights.theme: LLM agent safety and multi-agent systems
highlights.why: 通过从规划器中移除工具并让受信任模型编写经过验证的工具调用，提供了清晰的授权边界，解决智能体工具滥用问题。
highlights.key_result: 合同执行在产生变更的合同目标中命名了每个被更改的对象（56/56，相比意图可见审查的 2/16 和盲审的 4/54），并且在规划器捆绑了未被请求的工作时，在 27/30 次运行中完成主要任务，而意图可见审查为 16/30。其有 10/96 次未授权操作，与盲审相同，多于意图可见审查。
evidence: All 56/56 changed objects in contract execution are named in the goal of the contract that produced the change, compared with 2/16 in intent-visible review and 4/54 in blind review (Table ).

Three further contract execution runs have no code-accepted contract, because every contract they submitted quoted words the user never wrote and code rejected it; all three leave the task incomplete. Counting them, main-task completion is 27/30 for contract execution versus 16/30 for intent-visible review.

Contract execution has 10/96 unauthorized actions, the same count as blind review (six discordant prompts in each direction) and more than intent-visible review (ten prompts only under contract execution and two only under intent-visible review, p=0.039).

highlights.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
highlights.authors: Xingyang Li, Tianlang Zhao, Song Han et al.
highlights.theme: Efficient LLM inference and model compression
highlights.why: 智能体驱动的量化方案设计相比公开 PTQ 方案提高了准确率，但摘要被截断，报告的提升有限。
highlights.key_result: 在四个推理模型中，QDA 在 W4A16、W4A8 和 W3A16 下将准确率平均比最强公开方案分别提高了 0.9、1.4 和 2.2 个百分点，每次搜索使用 64 GPU-hours；在 NVFP4 W4A4 下的 320B 参数 MoE 模型 GLM-5.3-Flash 上，它恢复了 FP8 模型 98.3% 的准确率，而最佳供应商检查点为 96.9%。
evidence: Across four reasoning models, QDA improves accuracy over the strongest public recipe by 0.9, 1.4 and 2.2 percentage points on average at W4A16 , W4A8 and W3A16 , using 64 GPU-hours per search.
On the 320B-parameter MoE model GLM-5.3-Flash at NVFP4 W4A4, it recovers 98.3% of the FP8 model's accuracy, against 96.9% for the best vendor checkpoint.

highlights.title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
highlights.authors: Sachith Abeywickrama, Peiliang Gong, Emadeldeen Eldele et al.
highlights.why: 识别时间序列嵌入中的局部几何结构，并通过图表传输仅调整受影响区域，提供轻量级域增量。
highlights.key_result: 在每种到达条件下仅有 5% 标注校准数据且测试时无任何条件标识的情况下，PACT 在四条件轴承故障流上保持平均宏 F1 高于 0.95，并且在比较的方法中，PACT 在 FD、WISDM、HHAR 和 UCI-HAR 上取得了最高的最终 AMF_1，在 FD 和 WISDM 上相比最强基线分别提升了 11.15 和 8.34 个百分点。
evidence: With only 5% labeled calibration data per arriving condition and no condition identity at test time, PACT maintains an average macro-F1 above 0.95 across a four-condition bearing-fault stream.

Among the methods in Table , PACT achieved the highest final AMF_1 on FD, WISDM, HHAR, and UCI-HAR. Its largest gains were on FD and WISDM, where it exceeded the strongest baseline shown by 11.15 and 8.34 percentage points, respectively.

highlights.title: IDEA: Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit for Inference-Time Backdoor Detection in GUI Agents
highlights.authors: Zhizhuo Kou, Sizai Hou, Jian Yang et al.
highlights.why: 通过具有共形有限样本保证的意图-证据支配反转，在推理时检测 GUI 智能体中的后门激活。
highlights.key_result: 在 ε=0.01 时，IDEA 是唯一在所有五个家族上 TPR 超过 0.89 的检测器，具有最高的平均值（0.972，对比 PCA 残差的 0.894）和最高的最差家族 TPR（0.898，对比 0.580）。
evidence: At =0.01 IDEA is the only detector above 0.89 TPR on all five families, with the highest average (0.972 against 0.894 for the PCA residual) and the highest worst-family TPR (0.898 against 0.580).

news.title: The Silent Consensus
Research acceleration: The jagged frontier
How Sumitomo Life’s leaders helped teams adopt ChatGPT Enterprise
Inside the Codex sandbox
Introducing Gemini 4 Neon
news.summary: Google DeepMind 推出了 Gemini 4 Neon，定价为 $3 per million 输入 token（缓存 $0.15 per million），$15 per million 输出 token，上下文窗口为 1 million-token。它在 xhigh 思考级别上的 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 得分为 61，在 Vals Index 上得分为 70.9%（第 2 名），在 Legal Research Bench 和 Tax Agent Bench 上排名第 1，在 Terminal-Bench 4.1 上得分为 65.2%，在 Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index 上得分为 58.6，并在 Gemini API、AI Studio、Gemini for business 和 Google Antigravity 中推出。

news.title: Genie 4 is now available
news.summary: Google DeepMind 向 Project Genie 中符合条件的 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户推出了 Genie 4，增加了环境实时文本提示编辑、原生音频、创意智能体和社区画廊。Genie 3 也进行了更新，每次生成最长可达 3 分钟（原为 60 秒）、世界链和 360 度全景定位。

news.title: The Gemini app is now available on lower-memory Android devices.
news.summary: Google 在符合条件的 Android（Go edition）低内存设备上提供了 Gemini 应用，重新设计了应用架构，使核心体验能在内存较少的硬件上运行。功能包括超过 45 种语言的 Gemini Live 对话、基于相机的翻译和 Nano Banana 图像生成，并计划在 Transsion 等合作伙伴即将推出的设备上预装。

news.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now
Build Training-Ready Physical AI Datasets with Two Prompts in NVIDIA Cosmos
news.summary: NVIDIA 介绍了 Cosmos Data Factory，包括五个云原生蓝图和六个可组合技能，由智能体编排，只需两个提示即可构建数据集。NVIDIA 报告称，与传统方法相比，在配备八个 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU 的云服务器上测量，数据集组装速度最高可提升 60 倍，自动驾驶汽车场景生成成本降低 45 倍。

news.title: Tackling GPU Bottlenecks in Plane-Wave DFT with K-Point Batching and Mixed Precision
news.summary: NVIDIA 推出了 Daviator，这是一个 GPU 内核库，用于在 VASP 中批量处理 k 点和自旋操作，包括批量 Davidson 特征求解器，以及一个将敏感步骤保持在 FP64 的混合精度层。基准测试报告显示，与 CPU 执行相比，求解时间最多加快 22 倍，成本最多降低 75%，在 FP32:FP64 比率较高的 GPU 上端到端加速约 2 倍，可通过 INCAR 文件中的 LDAVIATOR 和 LDAVIATOR_MIXED_PRECISION 设置启用。

news.title: DaisyRose-27B: Pushing the Frontier of Post-Training Efficiency
news.summary: RadixArk 发布了 DaisyRose-27B，基于 Qwen3.8-27B 构建，并在 Miles 中使用强化学习在长达 1M token 的长时程智能体任务上训练，使用 1,200 个精选任务，在 144 个 H200 GPU 上历时 18 天。Terminal-Bench 4.1 的 pass@1 从 5.6% 提升至 12.0%，检查点以 Apache 2.0 协议发布，格式为 BF16、FP8 和 NVFP4，模型保留 256K-token 上下文窗口。

news.title: Why your fine-tuning job takes longer than the FLOPs say
news.summary: 一篇 Hugging Face 帖子预览了一篇关于预测端到端微调时间的论文，使用 272 个生产监督微调作业，在 NVIDIA H200 GPU 上总计约 7,382 GPU-hours。基于 FLOP 的估计达到 R² = 0.31，MAE 为 12.41 h；而仅使用预调度信息的 CatBoost 回归器在 5 折交叉验证中达到 R² = 0.98，平均绝对误差为 1.71 h，中位数误差为 0.51 h。

news.title: Time-Series Models in the Streamhouse: A New Frontier and Use Cases
news.summary: IBM 和 Confluent 将拥有超过 50 million 次下载的 IBM 时间序列基础模型原生集成到 Confluent 中，作为 Apache Flink 上的内置函数，可在 Confluent Cloud 和本地环境中的 CPU 上运行，无需 GPU。这些模型支持通过 SQL 对流数据进行预测、异常检测和语义智能。

news.title: Exa boosts embedding throughput by 50% to index billions of documents on AWS AI chips
news.summary: Exa 描述了在 AWS Neuron 硬件（Inferentia2 和 Trainium2）上优化其嵌入管线，报告相比朴素 FP16 数据并行基线约有 1.5 倍（即 50%）的吞吐量提升。优化包括权重布局更改和自动混合精度，降精度输出满足 0.999 余弦相似度正确性阈值；该工作始于对 30 billion 份高优先级文档进行重新嵌入。

news.title: Introducing workload recovery and expanded infrastructure checks on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
news.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod 增加了工作负载恢复和基础设施检查：MultiNodeTrainingValidation 在实例间训练一个小模型，并在出现 NaN 或无穷损失或超时时报错；还增加了 Kubernetes 资源监控代理和 Slurm 作业的挂起检测。该帖子引用 Meta 将 54 天 Llama 3 405B 预训练运行中 419 次意外中断中的 6 次归因于静默数据损坏。

news.title: Introducing the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard
news.summary: AWS 在 SageMaker Studio 中推出了 Amazon SageMaker JumpStart 模型排行榜，使用 AWS 运行的评估以及标准化测试工作负载的实测性能和成本指标，基于 BIG-Bench Hard、GPQA Diamond 和 MMLU-Pro 对模型进行排名。发布时覆盖来自 Meta、Google、Qwen、IBM 和 Arcee 等提供商的 70+ 个模型。

news.title: How Airbnb uses cost per task to operate coding agents on Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Airbnb described using cost per task, the list-price cost of all tokens an agent uses to finish one task, from evaluations on its own tasks to select models and reasoning-effort defaults for coding agents routed through its LLM gateway on Amazon Bedrock. The post notes eight new models came out in about five weeks, and by mid-October about two thirds of requests went to those new models.
